messages:
Arjun Patel: Hey team, unpacked my monitor and when I plug the USB-C into my M2 laptop the monitor powers on for ~3s then goes black and cycles. No image other than the monitor logo. Happens on both USB-C ports. Help?

alex-it: welcome Arjun! :wave: quick ask — is the monitor the 34\" ultrawide we shipped (model: RW-34U)? Can you try the HDMI cable in the box with the included USB-C power adapter plugged into the monitor and connect laptop via HDMI adapter just to isolate DP Alt Mode vs power issue?

Arjun Patel: yes RW-34U. Tried HDMI -> USB-C adapter (from kit) and the monitor gets a picture but it's really unstable (flicker every few seconds). When using HDMI the monitor says input HDMI1 and firmware shows v1.02 in the OSD.

alex-it: ok that suggests USB-C Alt Mode negotiation problem or bad cable. Two quick checks: 1) try a different USB-C cable rated for 40Gbps/alt-mode if you have one; 2) reset NVRAM and SMC on Mac (see commands below). If HDMI works but flickers, could be a bad HDMI cable or the monitor firmware — we can RMA if needed.

Arjun Patel: don't have another Thunderbolt cable here. Tried another HDMI cable from home and flicker still there. Ran the NVRAM reset per docs (hold Option+Cmd+P+R) and restarted, no change.

it-bot: Ticket created: IT-13045 for Arjun Patel (category: monitor/hardware). Priority: high (new hire, blocking dev setup). Assigned: alex-it. ETA spare processing: 2 business days.

alex-it: thanks. Please grab the monitor serial from the OSD (Settings > Info) and paste it so I can check warranty and recent firmware notes. Also run `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType` and paste the output so I can confirm what macOS sees when HDMI is connected.

Arjun Patel: serial is RW34U-GB-0921. system_profiler output (summarized):
```
Graphics/Displays:
  Intel Integrated Graphics:
    Chipset Model: Apple M2 Integrated
    Displays:
      RW-34U:
        Resolution: 3440 x 1440
        Connection Type: HDMI
        Main Display: Yes
        Mirror: Off
```
Monitor appears but flickers.

alex-it: good info. Given HDMI sometimes shows image but unstable and USB-C cycles, I'm leaning to faulty monitor unit or bad internal power board. Helen from ops, can we check spares in LON? Also request a courier pickup for return if replacement sent.

helen-ops: @shipping-bot check monitor RW-34U stock in LON warehouse. If available, package a replacement and mark as priority new-hire. Also include a return label for the defective unit (we'll do pickup).

shipping-bot: Replacement RW-34U available in LON stock (qty 2). Preparing priority shipment to Arjun Patel. Pickup scheduled for defective unit tomorrow morning. Tracking will be posted here once label created.

alex-it: plan: ship replacement overnight. When it arrives, test with the included TB4 cable first; if the replacement also fails, escalate to vendor warranty and swap to a different model. For now Arjun, you can use the laptop display or connect a borrowed monitor from the common kit (ask Facilities).

ryan-manager: thanks for the quick response team. Arjun, LMK if you need loaner desk or immediate swap so you can continue onboarding.

Arjun Patel: thanks all — appreciate the fast help. I'll grab a loaner if the replacement ETA is more than a day. Will update ticket IT-13045 when I get tracking.
